utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everybody in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of the Office of the Prosecutor, I'm Tom Hannis along with Jasmina Bosnjakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic, Igor Pantelic, and Aleksandar Aleksic appearing for Zupljanin Defence. Our client is not present. He already signed a waiver which I think we have it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. We have been alerted that before the witness comes in there are some matters which the OTP wishes to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, if I may, Your Honour. I have two matters and I think the first one I would like to go into private session for, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And we are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, the other matter relates to the exhibit that was MFI'd as P1608 yesterday. This was an excerpt from Mladic notebook, and I just wanted to make an apology to my learned friend Mr. Zecevic because yesterday I referred to him as my alleged learned friend in part because I didn't understand the basis of his objection and I took offence because I thought he was raising an inference that the Prosecution had made up this exhibit out of whole cloth with no basis. But his objection, now that I understand it, is well taken. We have not uploaded into e-court the original handwritten Cyrillic version of that excerpt of the diary and that should be it. We will upload it with the Court's permission to do that, and with that that's my apology to Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. In terms of the comity which is necessary for the courts to function properly, I'm sure that the Chamber even before Mr. Zecevic acknowledges your apology is grateful for your explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to thank Mr. Hannis for the apology and for the explanation. I made the objection yesterday obviously -- I wasn't successful as Your Honours recall with my objection, but now I think we have discussed it afterwards and we will remedy the situation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And with that, Your Honour, I'm ready to resume with the witness if there's nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we'll lower the blinds so the witness may take the stand. Sorry, before we do that, the -- we go back into private session so matters to which the Chamber would speak.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Chamber notes that we are coming towards the end of the most recent batting order for Prosecution witnesses, and we will appreciate receiving the order for October to the end of the Prosecution's case. Is it possible to provide that by the end of this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I know Ms. Pidwell has a provisional batting order for the remaining witnesses that's been circulated within the team. I think there were a couple of witnesses that we're trying to confirm for the dates in question, but that's something that we could provide to you I would say probably tomorrow. I think Ms. Pidwell's gone home this afternoon, but I think we could get that to you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Related to that, the Chamber notes that the Prosecution has today made a filing notifying the Chamber of pre-existing protective measures which apply to 13 witnesses still to be called. Asking first the Prosecution, is it intended to call any of these witnesses before the middle of October so that expedited responses from the Defence, if any, are needed? And the second question is to the Defence, whether they do intend to respond to the notification at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to the first question, Your Honour, again I have to confer with Ms. Pidwell. I might be able to find out that information this afternoon or otherwise I can advise you tomorrow if that's adequate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we do intend to respond to this motion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. So we'll have to wait for the response from the Prosecution tomorrow. And last matter, on the 17th of September, 2010, Zupljanin Defence document was marked for identification pending translation. We understand that the translation is now available and so the document can be de-MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, just confirm it's 2D110.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We have it on the record now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document in question, Your Honours, is 2D110 MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. The -- now we lower the blinds so the witness can be escorted back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir. Good afternoon to you, sir. Before I invite Mr. Hannis to resume his examination-in-chief, I remind you you're still on your oath. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. I only have a few questions left for you, and I think I need to go in private session for the first couple as they may touch on your identity.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And we are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In September or October of 1992, did you have occasion to travel to Visegrad municipality?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on that occasion did you see what appeared to be to you some sort of paramilitary formation in the town?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us about that. What did they look like? Did you ask anybody who it was? What did you learn about them?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of a building from which a black flag flew I saw a group of people, and I asked the president of the municipality of Visegrad who was with me who those people were, and he told me -- I think his name is Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this black flag looked like? Was it a simple plain black flag or was there any kind of emblem on it?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a flag with a skull.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you remember the first name of the Mr. Lukic you were told about?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think his first name was Milan, Milan Lukic or some such.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And from whom did you get the information about this group? Who told you about them?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brano Savovic, the president of Visegrad municipality told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could show the witness 65 ter 1467.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Coming on your screen in a moment, Witness, is a document that appears to be a military telegram dated the 10th of September, 1992. And it says -- my English translation says: "At the request of representatives of Zvornik Serb municipality and the SJB and with the aim of resolving the issue of the collection centre in Divic and releasing the civilian population of Muslim nationality that are at the collection centre to the territory of Kalesija and Kladanj, they are asking to be authorised the possibility of transferring these people to the above territories through the light infantry brigade." Did you know that there were still Muslim civilians detained in Divic in September of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you know what authorities from Zvornik Serb municipality would have made this request?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. One last question just to clarify something that was discussed yesterday. At transcript page 14861, I don't know if you will remember, we were looking at the document that formed the Crisis Staff in December of 1991. And I'd asked you if you could help me with a couple of acronyms at the bottom of the page where it said any political negotiations with the SDA were forbidden except for people who were authorised to do so by GO, and your answer said GO stands for Executive Board. My question: Is that the same thing as what's occasionally referred to as the Main Board of the SDS, at the highest level of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we spoke about that referring to the municipality rather than the Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we can show the witness Exhibit P436.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, I just want to be sure I am clear about this. And the other acronym was MO, which I think you said stood for local boards.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Local board, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So in the context of this document, does that mean local boards within Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zvornik municipality there was a Municipal Board which some people also called Main Board, and in addition there were local boards. So there were local boards and Municipal Boards. And this abbreviation stood for the members of the Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And "GO" means the Executive Board of the SDS in Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. Since this was a document of the municipality, the reference was to the members of the local board and of the Municipal Board. The Municipal Board is a higher-ranking body than the local board.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I'm sorry, "GO" refers to what, the Executive Board of the SDS in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. I don't have any further questions for you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm about to start with a general question. If you could, as it were, order the events in Zvornik and classify them in time and in place, could you perhaps make a -- make a ladder of events for us to be able to orient ourselves?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to structure the political activities in Zvornik, I would structure it in three parts. The first phase would be from the elections to the establishment of the joint bodies in Bosnia-Herzegovina at municipal level. That went on until the end of 1991. The second phase is the beginning of the end of the functioning of the authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which went from the end of 1991 to the beginning of 1992. And the third phase would be the war in which there was complete anarchy until the arrest of the paramilitaries in Zvornik, and only then did government start functioning in Zvornik municipality, government or state authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let us be more precise. If you agree with me, we will limit that war time-period from the 6th of April until the arrival of the special unit, right?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm not so much interested in the first period but the second period of the crumbling of authorities in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Could you make a list of the causes of the crisis but without a deep analysis?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it's well-known to everybody. There was Yugoslavia as a joint state. Bosnia-Herzegovina was an integral part of Yugoslavia. (redacted), from the very first moment until it ceased to work, practically half the time was used to deal with the issues of tackling the crisis in former Yugoslavia without its affecting Bosnia-Herzegovina and its breakup. And the effect was the following. Decisions were taken to mitigate what was the consequence of the demands of the Muslims and the Croats to nullify everything that originated from the federal level. And so the proposal was formulated that the Serbs -- or rather, that Bosnia-Herzegovina remain in a joint state and that some democratic matters should be defined that would make possible good relations among the ethnicities. There was also the proposal to establish a council of peoples where there would be no down-voting of any side and where essential issues could be regulated, and all that was part of the Cutileiro Plan which was also signed. However, the plan didn't come into effect and Bosnia-Herzegovina basically ceased to exist and the authorities fell apart. As a consequence, many people started appearing at places where they didn't belong. There were people who had doubtful qualities. Everything was based on the ethnic -- was based on ethnicity, on ethnic grounds. A big problem was the conflict with the JNA. The Muslims and Croats were attacking it, whereas we still saw it as a joint army, the task of which was to preserve the peace in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Yugoslavia. Of course that had an effect on Zvornik municipality too. From the level of the republic, the problem descended to the municipalities. That would be it in a nutshell.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show 1D03, on the screens, 4415. Let us move to the following page immediately, where we will see the contents. The following page. Right. Let us enlarge the right half and we also need the English version. I think that we have both versions now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can see here the decisions of the Crisis Staff. The first one is the decision on the declaration of the state of war in the territory of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik. You commented that yesterday; correct? Now the second decision is the decision regarding restrictions on the disposal of strategic stockpile. Do you remember that the Crisis Staff adopted this decision?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say anything about particular about it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The introduction of work obligation, I believe that you said something about that to the Prosecutor yesterday, and the decision on the introduction of a curfew. There's also the decision on the establishment of a provisional government. Can you see it? And it says down there that the Crisis Staff also issued some orders, such as the order on general mobilisation, the order on the marking of vehicles, and the order on the mobilisation of civilians. After that you can see the enactments of the provisional government?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that these basic strategic decisions were first adopted by the Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: After that the provisional government took over power in Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: And the provisional government continued to make all crucial decisions; correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this gazette with all regulations is a very lengthy document. I only asked to -- for its contents to be displayed so that we may see the extent of the legislative activities of the authorities in Zvornik municipality. And since the table of contents is a relatively small portion of the entire document, I seek to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- we were just wondering, Mr. Cvijetic, whether the nature of this document is not such that it could be conveniently placed in the law library. I take your point about seeking only to tender the page in interest of economy, but I see certain practical problems about that course. Does the Prosecution have a view on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have any question about the authenticity of this, and particular enactments may be something relevant and I'd like to argue about it at the end of the case, and I think your suggestion to perhaps add it to the law library is something that would be acceptable to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will accept this suggestion and I will move on. That it becomes part of the law library. Can we now look at 1D03-4368, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, I didn't want to repeat this. You saw the decision on the declaration of the state of war in the municipality of Zvornik, and then on the same day the order on general mobilisation was adopted. Do you recall that order?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is from day three -- actually, the 8th of April. I cannot remember specifically, but I don't dispute that it was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Adopted at a meeting of the Crisis Staff. I'm asking you that because you were a member of the Crisis Staff. Can you confirm the authenticity of this document?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm its authenticity, but I'm not disputing that a decision of this nature was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Just like the decision on the declaration of the state of war?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I rise just to perhaps out of an abundance of caution suggest that we have a redaction there with the identification of the witness as being a member of a small body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't mind moving into private session because I'm going to be showing other documents of this small body, so perhaps there would be no need then to redact the transcript. I do accept your suggestion, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, perhaps it would be better to move into private session. I'm going to be going through all the documents now of the Crisis Staff and some other documents, so perhaps it would be wiser to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It appears that that's simpler at this stage.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us again the name of the president because the transcript is incorrect. Could you say it slowly.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the temporary government is Branko Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: If you're able to recall, can you please tell us who the other members were; and if you speak slowly because of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can remember is that the secretary of national defence was still Stevo Ivanovic. One of the members was Stevo Radic. I do not really remember the others. I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document because I think it's very relevant to the events in Zvornik. I would like to tender that as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D378, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: We're going to look at two documents now, two exhibits -- or actually, two decisions -- actually, a number of decisions of the government, the temporary government.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we look at 1D03-4378. We need to look at the right-hand side of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, this is a decision of the temporary government on the establishment of a special unit of the Territorial Defence. You can read the contents, just acquaint yourself with the contents of the decision. Are you aware on the basis of this decision or on the basis of your personal knowledge what the unit was that was granted this special status?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this decision was adopted on the establishment of the special unit?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: All right. Then I'm going to remind you about what unit this is and I'm going to do that with our next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we look at 1D03-4403 instead of this one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You can see here what this unit is precisely. Pursuant to this approval, the temporary government secured funds for the procurement of uniforms. That refers to the Igor Markovic unit. Are you aware that that was one of the names of the unit that was under the command of Zuco?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The temporary government thus was financing one of the volunteer units. Are you aware of this information, that it was being financed through the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was aware that there were payments through the Territorial Defence because I had the opportunity to see that in certain documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these are two very important decisions from the Zvornik municipality area, and I believe that we have reason to adopt this document also on the approval on the establishment of the special TO unit and also this one on the approval for the provision of materiel and manufacture of uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the record, the previous document, I don't think any of the witness's answers justified getting that document in. However, I'm satisfied regarding the authenticity of both these documents. We -- these are documents the OTP received from sources that lead us to feel quite comfortable that these are authentic and were made at the time and say what they say on the screen. So I don't object to admission of either one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D379, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to repeat, there were two documents. I have to repeat, there were two documents. I am talking about the first document, 1D03-4378 is a decision on the establishment of the unit; and the second document, 1D03-4403, on the procurement of equipment and uniforms for the special units -- unit. So I think the two documents are connected. This is why I wanted to tender them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I have no objection except to indicate that the last document I see only refers to supply of fabrics from manufacturing uniforms and no reference to equipment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for clarification, Your Honours, document 1D03-4378 will be Exhibit 1D379 and document 1D03-4403 will be 1D380, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I'm just curious about what it is you're seeking to show with these two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I intend to show just three or four more documents, and I would like to deal with the -- I would like to proceed by subject matter that the provisional government dealt with. It is our submission which I'll put briefly. The provisional government took decisions that were within the remit of the state. In Zvornik a situation was created that Zvornik became a state within a state. It had its army, its police, its government, they take decisions from the remit of the state; and now I proceed by subject matter. I have now arrived at the judiciary and I have one or two more decisions and I will finish this topic with -- just with two or three more documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, if I may, before we proceed, you're saying that the provisional government of the TO established a special unit, the purpose of which was to secure the territory of the Serbian areas in Zvornik. And then you move on to show another document that suggests that Igor Markovic, who was in command of some of the volunteer groups under Zuco, was put in charge of the special unit. So you're proving a link between the governments and the volunteer groups; is that correct or have I misunderstood?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You understood correctly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I need to then interject and ask a question because I'm not sure who Igor Markovic was. And I don't know that we've had evidence that he was the commander of any unit. I think the unit was named for this person, but I think that was somebody who was killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You are correct indeed, Mr. Hannis. But my question was merely whether Mr. Zecevic [sic], through the witness, was trying to show that the provisional government in Zvornik was financing the activities of a volunteer unit. And I understood his answer to be positive.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We have seen evidence from witnesses who were in Zvornik and we have also seen payrolls, so that is not a contested issue. Earlier evidence has shown that the unit in question was named after a member of that unit who was killed, and that is this volunteer unit commanded by Zuco. May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see document 1D03-4381. I apologise, the left-hand side of the document is what we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a decision of the provisional government dated 27 April about the disengagement of the judicial -- of judicial staff at the Public Prosecutor's Office in Zvornik. Do you know that such a decision was adopted?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that it was adopted. I cannot confirm its authenticity, but I also do not contest that it was adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you the same question about all decisions, but please focus your attention on the introduction. The provisional government bases all its decisions on Article 5 of the decision on the declaration of the state of war; can you see that? On the left side at the top.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So can you confirm that the provisional government relied exclusively on the decision on the declaration of the state of war in the adoption of all of its decisions? We have seen that on all documents.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're a lawyer so you're better qualified than me to see that it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that this is a very important decision. I seek to tender it and I will proceed to show another important decision that affects the judiciary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I see from your last question to the witness with which -- to which the witness demurred is, I assume, the alert to the Chamber of an argument which you're going to make at the end of the exercise, and it is to that end that you are using these documents as foundation for argument, rather than purporting for there to be any nexus between the document and the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the foundation for tendering this document -- these documents is the fact that the Crisis Staff decided to declare the state of war, and based on that the provisional government adopted a series of decisions that are extremely important and they basically show that the state of war was indeed in effect in Zvornik municipality. And the witness was in Zvornik throughout the period I cannot now say as to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D381, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following document: 1D03-4407. It's the right-hand side that we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, here too we see why the previous decision was adopted. We saw there that persons holding positions of the regular court and Public Prosecutor's Office were replaced, and here we see that a war time military court is being established. Do you know that this was the case? And we also see here that this is based on the decision of the declaration of the state of war.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I cannot confirm the authenticity. But I believe that such a decision existed, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: So you allow for the possibility of the existence of this decision?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, looking at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I would just like to hear whether you know who the president of the war time military court was?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I must seek to tender this document because it belongs with the previous one because once the regular court and the Public Prosecutor's Office were replaced, were no longer in function, now a war time military court was established. And this is the basis for my subsequent dealings with the witness; that's why I seek to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, logically I suppose we having admitted the previous document it would be odd not to admit this, but the witness himself has used a word which the Chamber itself didn't articulate before and which is relevant to the admissibility of this document as well as the previous document and that is the word "authenticity." Could you assist us in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, these documents -- was disclosed before and I only have documents contained in the Official Gazette of the municipality of Zvornik. Issue 2 and issue 3 contain these decisions, and the witness himself doesn't doubt its authenticity. We received the documents that -- because the Prosecution disclosed them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot confirm that they are authentic. I can only say that I think they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you have any idea as to how this court was going to function and who would be the other members of the court? Or was this all left with Captain Stanojevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not a member of the provisional government. I do not know the intention of this document or this decision. I don't know what its purpose was, nor do I know how the decision was implemented, and I don't know the man either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour. Again, I don't have a question about authenticity because these documents are part of the greater collection that was received by us all at the same time and they appear to be related and consistent with other evidence that's in this case and perhaps other evidence that I may know from another case, but I'm not contesting authenticity. But the last two documents, the relevance of them at this point is less clear to me than some of the earlier ones. And part of my objection is the way the questions are asked and the way it's presented to the witness, where Mr. Cvijetic is partly testifying about what this document means and what it shows about how that court was done away with and this one was established for that purpose. And this witness doesn't know and he hasn't been able to comment to that effect. And I don't want at the end of the case Mr. Cvijetic jumping up and pointing to these documents and saying, "See, these show what I said they show." Well, he's not a witness, so they don't show that. So I don't have an objection about authenticity and I can see that some inferences and arguments can be made, but not to the level Mr. Cvijetic is putting for them at this point. So other than that I don't know how you want to proceed with it, but that's my question, the relevance isn't so obvious to me about these last two yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, as I said, having admitted the previous document, it would be awkward not to admit this, so this too is admitted and marked. But in terms of your last observation, Mr. Hannis, the only way I can say it is you can trust the Chamber in analysing the evidence to separate evidence from submissions disguised as questions.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Admitted as Exhibit 1D382, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not sure when the break is due, but possibly now would be a convenient time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think it's 3.40, which is about seven minutes away, but if you feel it is convenient to do it now we could as easily take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine with me. I can also continue, but all right we can have the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cvijetic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please bear with me, Your Honour. I'm getting tangled in all this technology.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, I think yesterday you were shown a document about the establishment of the TO command in the Serb municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just in case, could we please have P1605 - I hope that's the correct number. It used to be 65 ter 2605. We need the left-hand side of the document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, I also wanted to double-check, and this was tendered yesterday through you, do you recall having seen this document which is a decision to form the Territorial Defence command of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik. It was issued by the provisional government. In Article 1 it is stated that Mr. Marko Pavlovic is appointed commander of that Territorial Defence. Do you remember being asked about this document by the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I won't dwell on it any further because it's already an exhibit. Rather, I will try to go through other two documents with you to see how this TO commander changed his positions in the municipality of Zvornik. Let's look at another document, which is P317.6. Witness, you can see here that this is a document of the military command of the East Bosnia Corps. It is signed by Colonel Nikola Dencic. We can see that this document establishes the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. Were you aware of such a brigade being established?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then I believe you're also familiar with the next fact, which is something you mentioned in your statement, and that is that it was formed out of members of the TO and that the Zvornik TO actually made part of this new brigade?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you're correct. The infantry brigade was established by the army. I don't know how, when, and where, but it wasn't the TO that established it; that is certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Then I'm afraid you misunderstood me. I wasn't trying to assert that. I'm only asserting that some -- as we can see from the decision that the TO HQ is to be transformed into the command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess it is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Therefore, this clarifies it. The army established that brigade by incorporating the TO HQ in Zvornik into its force?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As you can see further down the decision a hand-over is referred to, to be executed by Major Marko-Branko Popovic, who was the current commander, and he was appointed to another position which was liaison officer with the FRY. Is this not Marko Pavlovic or his other name?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear that he came under an assumed name or a false name. Somewhere I seem to have read that his first name was Branko, although I'm not positive. In any case, this may well be the case, as is stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. We can see that this was done on May 30th, 1992, when he was to move to his new position within a military unit. Can we see that in the document, in particular in item 3?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: He was supposed to move to another duty in the east --

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well. I wanted to show you the last document concerning this man. It is already an exhibit -- sorry, I'll -- the next one I'm about to show is not an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D03-4408, the left-hand side of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, you see here that the provisional government later on, after this attempt to move Mr. Pavlovic to the military unit on the 16th of June, issued this decision to appoint commander of the unified military territorial command of the Serb municipality of Zvornik. As you can see at item III, again Marko Pavlovic is being appointed commander. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that Mr. Marko Pavlovic, following the establishment of the brigade, remained in the territory of the municipality of Zvornik and he was assigned a new duty by the provisional government?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that after the Zvornik Brigade was established, he did not leave Zvornik immediately, although I don't know where he was at that time and what his position was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I'm a little bit confused here. Is it your position that the Marko Pavlovic is the same man as the Marko - what was it? - Marko-Branko Popovic in the previous document? Does the witness confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, given that this line of document relies on the document we saw yesterday whereby he was appointed commander of the TO HQ, I want to tender this document as well because it indicates how he moved from one position to the next in the territory of the municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D383, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, by virtue of these documents I wanted to deal with a period --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. Didn't that already have an exhibit number? Okay. Which one are we talking about because I thought that we were talking about the Marko Pavlovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Tab 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The previous document referred to by Judge Delvoie is already an exhibit and I tendered this last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, by virtue of these documents I wanted to cover a period in Zvornik between the 6th of April and the establishment or the introduction of the special police unit in the area. Would you agree with me that Zvornik with its provisional government during that period functioned as a mini state basically?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 6th of April and the arrival of the special brigade, republican authorities basically did not have any power in that area. They did not function.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you were asked something about the police station chief, and at a certain point you told my learned friend that it was precisely during that period that position was held by Mr. Milos Pantelic who hails from Loznica and not from Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Since you said that the central authorities of Republika Srpska held no sway over what was happening in Zvornik, another way to corroborate that is to show what we did and that is that it was basically the local authorities who appointed commanders in the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the last period then. Can you recall when the special unit entered Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They entered Zvornik either in late April --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- late July or early August, although I don't recall the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It suffices. As I asked you about the previous period, can you briefly explain this period following the arrival of that unit. Were there any changes?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the moment of their arrival in Zvornik, the first thing that was done was to cleanse Zvornik of most paramilitary formations. Most of them were arrested and taken to the prison in Bijeljina. The rest took to their heels and some took shelter in certain units. As of that moment, they could no longer function as a unit or a group. As of that moment in Zvornik there were basically no paramilitary formations as units and they had no influence over any authorities. The second thing that happened was that immediately following that we held a session of the Municipal Assembly -- let me resume. After that we had a quiet period when the Municipal Assembly could sit in order to fulfil the order of the president to establish functioning civilian municipal organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, with the arrival of the special unit a new person was appointed the police chief by a decision of the minister of the interior. Did you know that person?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Can you give us an overview or assessment of his work after he assumed his duty?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot. I did not control or supervise his work. What I do need to say, though, is that from the outset he was simply in a situation which allowed him to organise and staff and equip the MUP of Republika Srpska so that the police could exercise its proper duties. In other words, he was able to pull his men back from the combat activities and duties they had been assigned to earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Were his efforts fruitful? Were there any results?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could feel the results immediately. As of that moment on, the police became better and better. They were able to do their job. Another important thing is this, during that period the judiciary became functional, fully functional. As of that moment there were no longer any collection centres run by paramilitaries. As of that moment, those who were detained were either moved to the central prison or to military jails. In other words, they were supervised.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you discussed with the Prosecutor your decision -- or rather, not your decision but the decision of the Serb municipality of Bratunac to establish -- apologies. Not Bratunac. The Serb municipality --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, before you go to another topic, it strikes me that we don't have here on the record the name of that new person that was appointed chief of the police. Can you ask the witness the name of that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Witness, you heard the question.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think his name was Mico Lokancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mico could be a nickname and his full name could be Milorad?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we knew him as Mico Lokancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm going to remind you now about what you said when talking to the Prosecutor, and you said with the arrival of the units these collection centres were abolished and that the Assembly adopted a decision on the formation of the municipal prison in Zvornik. You mentioned yesterday the adoption of such a decision; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: However, I think that yesterday you had a difference with the Prosecutor about the date of the adoption of the decision on the establishment of the municipal prison in Zvornik. The Prosecutor said that he didn't have that document on hand at the time. I think I will show you a document that I think is the one. It's 1D04 - we submitted the document for translation - document 2983. And you can see it here. I must admit, my learned friend the Prosecutor is correct. He did refer to this date yesterday, the 19th of August, 1992. So can you correct yourself in that sense, do you agree with these assertions?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Is this the document that you discussed with the Prosecutor yesterday about the establishment of the prison?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document. For the moment we can just mark it for identification. We were promised by the translation unit that they would have a translation of it for us by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sorry, no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we'll mark it for identification pending the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D384, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What was the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0179-8584.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can this be done in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree. I wasn't careful enough. I agree. We need to move to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I would indicate it appears we're going to be finishing well before 7.00. I am advised that the next witness, the Prosecution would request that we not begin with her until tomorrow morning no matter when we finish today because she has just arrived, there's been extensive proofing, and I think she and the Prosecutor would prefer that. I have discussed it with Defence counsel and I think they have no disagreement with that, if it's okay with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, I would first like to ask you about a document that Mr. Cvijetic showed you, it is 1D382, if we could have that up. This is a document that was the - it's the right-hand page I believe - the decision on the establishment of the war time military court. Do you know, Witness, if such a court indeed was actually established and ever functioned in Zvornik in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember that a court like that existed in Zvornik in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next if we could look at Exhibit P317.6 I believe. It was tab 26 of the Defence binder. Yes. You were shown this document from Colonel Dencic. Item number 1 transforms the municipal TO HQ into the command of the Zvornik Infantry Brigade. Number 2 says: "Hand-over or take-over of duty between the TO commander and the newly appointed commander of the infantry brigade is to be carried out ..." on a certain date. Now, we understand -- am I correct in understanding that at that time on the 30th of May, 1992, the Zvornik municipal TO commander was Marko Pavlovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the 30th of May, according to this decision, Marko Pavlovic was the commander. Based on this decision, someone else should have taken over starting on the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. And it makes reference to a newly appointed commander of the infantry brigade. Do you know who that person was?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At one point in Zvornik the brigade commander was Lieutenant-Colonel, I think his name was, Vasilic. Now, whether he was appointed by Dencic or not. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know what date he held that position?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Item number 3 which gives us information indicating that Marko Pavlovic's true name was Branko Popovic, and it looks like apparently that's something that Colonel Dencic and the East Bosnia Corps knew, but in Zvornik in the municipal government in town you only knew him as Marko Pavlovic; correct? That's the name that appears on the TO pay sheet, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Item number 3 says he's to be the officer for liaison with the FRY, with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Do you know if Marko Pavlovic actually took up such a position and what the duties involved?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I don't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Wasn't Marko Pavlovic after the 30th of June -- after the 30th of May, 1992, still actively involved in directing some armed forces in Zvornik, for example, in Kozluk in late June?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During our earlier conversations I was saying that even after the establishment of the Zvornik Brigade, Marko Pavlovic remained in Zvornik for some period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And he was involved in directing armed forces; yes?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know what he was involved in. I don't even know whether this order was implemented fully, because at one point both Marko Pavlovic and Lieutenant-Colonel Vasilic were present in Zvornik. Who was in charge of what, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, you told us yesterday about the people from Djulici who wanted to leave and you'd been involved in those discussions and how you were away when they actually left. You came back and found out that Marko Pavlovic had had the military-aged men taken out of that group of people wanting to leave and detained them, and you had an argument with him about that; right?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look at 1D383.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were also shown this one by Mr. Cvijetic. It's dated I think the 16th of June and it's a provisional government decision on establishment of the single military and territorial command, so some two weeks plus after that document we just looked at. And now the provisional government in item III says that: "Marko Pavlovic has been appointed for commander of this military and territorial command." What is this body that's being talked about? This is not the Zvornik Brigade, is it?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the document, it was not the Zvornik Brigade, but I really don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, item II says: "Organisation, combat-readiness, single command, and combat use of independent formations ..." Do you know who those people were?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At page 35, line 9, you were asked about the new police [Realtime transcript read in error "political"] chief, Lokancevic's efforts, when he took up the job in August. And you mentioned that you could feel the results immediately and that things got better in Zvornik. You said: "As of that moment those who were detained were either moved to the central prison or to the military jails." But you remember we looked at a document this morning that showed us as of the 10th of September there were still a number of Muslim civilians detained in Divic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember having been shown that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And do you remember that people actually still were in detention in Divic in September?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's okay. At page 43, line 14, you were asked about the operation carried out to round-up the Yellow Wasps and the other groups in late July 1992. Were you aware that that round-up was conducted not only by Mr. Karisik's special unit but also by members of a special unit of the federal MUP led by Milorad Davidovic, did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did you know it also included members of the VRS --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Zecevic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to correct the transcript. On page 54, 19, it is recorded the new political chief. I think you said the police chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that's clear and we'll leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know if you were able to answer my question about whether you know members of the VRS also participated in the round-up of the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the VRS and their role.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Lastly I want to ask you about the meeting in Sekovici where you informed Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Mandic about the problems and the crimes that you were aware of that had been taking place in Zvornik. And if I may, I'd like to hand you a hard copy of your statement from 1992 [sic], and if you could -- I've put a little blue sticky on the page where I want you to turn to. Paragraph 130 if you find it.

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in answering Mr. Cvijetic's questions about when that date may have been just earlier this afternoon, you said that you had said it was several weeks and you were now allowing for the possibility that it was in June. But yesterday when I asked you about this at page 14889, line 10, I said: "Q. In terms of the date of the meeting in Sekovici, in your statement in 2002 you indicated it was a few weeks after the start of the war. Is that still -- was that still your memory?" And yesterday you said: "Yes." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ST-215 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several weeks I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No. I'm reading the transcript. You said "a few weeks."

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to be fair to the witness, he should be presented with all of his answers. He said initially late in May, then he said several weeks -- he didn't say couple of weeks. And my colleague Mr. Zecevic is telling me that it's page 14860 page. And then later on he said several weeks. And finally he allowed for the number I put to him. I think the witness should be presented with all the answers he had provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, that would have been good to do on cross-examination as well. And the point I'm asking about is page 14889, which was some 29 pages after the others, after I'd gone through some things with him to try to get him to see if reading his statement refreshed his memory about what he said in 2002, which is where he said "a few weeks."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But in any event, I'm lost as to what turns on this, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to discuss it in front of the witness because he understands a fair bit of English, but I can explain to you why I think it's important and you'll see the Defence thinks it's important too. That's why they spent so much time on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So, Mr. Witness, how many weeks after the meeting was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the first occasion I said "several weeks." However, while giving answers to both sides I was not at the time certain of the date when the events took place. I allowed for the possibility of it having happened in late May or early June, as I was told by the Defence lawyer. But I'm not certain myself. I didn't write it down anywhere. I really cannot say that with any degree of certainty. I wouldn't know what date it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I continue or do you want to hear my argument about why I'm spending so much time on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, not yet, but I don't think we'll get any closer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- given the witness's last answer to Judge Harhoff's question, in summary what he has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, in summary, Your Honour, one of the things I need to clear up is his answer just now, he said, "on the first occasion I said 'several weeks.'" I need to ask him what first occasion he's talking about because the first occasion I have a record of is the June 2002 statement in which he said "a few weeks."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But I'm looking at his answer. "I am not sure myself. I didn't write it down anywhere. I really cannot say with any degree of certainty. I wouldn't know what date it was." Is pressing him going to get us any further on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to establish a certain chronology concerning what answers he's made about that and an argument to be made from it, but I don't think I should do it in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, if you insist, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- I am looking at the time and I'm wondering how most efficiently to handle this. Should we take the adjournment now and then when we resume the -- have you deal with this before the witness is escorted back to the stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Either that or we could take him out now and I could speak for 10 or 15 minutes and then we could take the recess and resume with the witness after we've decided how much and to what extent I'm allowed to go further into it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Okay. Well, the latter course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I really do apologise, Your Honours. If my learned friend Mr. Hannis is intending to speak 10 or 15 minutes, I think it's almost for final arguments not for -- why 15 minutes' discussion? And I really do apologise. I'm a little bit concerned which kind of submissions you will make for 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think Your Honours should wait and hear what I have to say and decide whether five minutes or 10 minutes or 15 minutes is enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The reason that the Prosecution views the question of this date is important is that the earlier the date this witness is giving information to the accused Mico Stanisic about crimes being committed in Zvornik, the more important that is because no action was taken in Zvornik until the end of July. And you've heard us say before that that really only took place after Minister Ostojic was taken out by the yellow wasps and put on the ground, not because crimes were happening against non-Serbs and Muslims. I think from the Defence point of view the later it happens and the closer to July the better it is for their position. And what I'm trying to say is when this witness was first asked about the timing of that event in his written statement in 2002 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, but if I may interrupt you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think I see where you're headed. At the end of the day, what the evidence is is the witness's testimony. The fact that on a previous occasion he may -- or on previous occasions he may have given -- been more precise or given different dates doesn't alter the fact that what we are left with is what he says is, "I really cannot, as I testify today, remember what it is." And I don't know that there's provision for either side, in this case what you would be seeking to argue to do, to substitute what he would have said on a previous occasion for his testimony in the box. That's why I ask -- I don't see -- that's why I'm asking what is the point of this exercise in which we're engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but in citing that question for yourselves and assessing his credibility, you will look at what he said and when he said it, what his motivation was at that time, what information he had, is his memory better in 2002 as opposed to 2010. And he did say yesterday in a question from me, you indicated it was a few weeks after the start of the war, is that still your memory? He said yes. That's what he said yesterday. And the chronology I'm trying to fill in is that in 2002 he said that in his written statement. In 2003 there was a taped interview with the Prosecution. He made no change to it. In proofing with him Friday, when the investigator had proofed him, I specifically asked him about paragraph 130, and you'll -- I think you'll probably get copied on the proofing note, he made no substantive changes to his statement. And then on Saturday he met with Mr. Cvijetic alone for the Defence proofing, and now he's saying, "Oh, maybe it was June, and it was several weeks." No, that's a factor for you to consider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Gentlemen, please. But, Mr. Hannis, with respect, the -- whatever the sequence at the end of the day, aren't we left with a witness -- aren't we left with testimony from the mouth of this witness which is unreliable to the -- in the sense that the -- insofar as this is a point which is of major importance for the Prosecution that the effect of the testimony of this witness is that it is so unreliable the Prosecution must be looking somewhere else in order to establish this fact? And the -- I know what Mr. -- well, I believe I know what Mr. Zecevic and Mr. Cvijetic were about to say, but the -- it isn't necessary for them to respond. I mean, the answer -- the suggestion -- the implication -- the -- what's the rule ? Post hoc ergo propter, you're falling into that trap.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but this witness requested protective measures and he told you one of the reasons that he wanted protective measures was because Serbs who testify against Serbs at the Tribunal are viewed as traitors. Set aside -- no suggestion of improper conduct on the part of the Defence. The mere fact that he's here and he's being questioned by Serb attorneys for Serb accused in The Hague is a factor that you may think about whether or not that influences him in answering those questions. That's -- I think that's a legitimate factor for you to consider. And I would just like to put the chronology in the record or at least put in paragraphs 130 and 131 from his statement so you see what he said the first time he was asked it where he had no concern about speaking in court and no reason to be fabricating the date at a point in time that was years closer to the events than we are today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will try. First of all, it's quite clear the witness is very clear throughout his testimony and in his previous statements he said "several weeks." After that he told Mr. Hannis that this was in May, that it was in late May, he allowed for the possibility that it was in June. And particularly we put it in the context of the liberation of Crni Vrh. So Mr. Hannis can say when the passage was cleared between Zvornik and Sekovici via Crni Vrh, and then we will know that the meeting took place after that date. It's quite simple. So I don't see why -- I really think it's not proper to mistreat the witness even though it's a Prosecution witness. As for all the other situations, the conduct of Serbian lawyers, Serbian witnesses, I really believe that comments like that are inappropriate because if that is the position then what are we going to say because that position can apply to members of other ethnic groups who come to testify here. That means if a person is a Muslim or a Croat, then by the very nature of things, according to what Mr. Hannis says that person would hate Serbs or their testimony should not believed. So I really don't see any consistency in the position of the Prosecution on this matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I agree with you, Mr. Zecevic, that I think that Mr. Hannis's comments in that regard were ill-advised. In the Chamber's view this matter has been taken as far as it can go. No useful purpose would be served by pressing the witness further on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Although it is obviously a live issue as to when the passage was cleared, but as I indicated earlier to the extent that there is controversy on the point of this witness's evidence is imprecise taken at its highest, it is something on which when the time comes for all of the evidence to be stitched together, the -- I would expect that the Chamber would be directed to evidence other than from this witness on that point. So we would take the adjournment now and come back to complete the re-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I asked to address you before the witness was brought in because I want you to know, Your Honours, and, Mr. President, that I take to heart your comment about my comments being ill-advised, and I apologise to my colleagues across the way if I gave offence. I didn't mean to. By analogy the point I was trying to make in America in a civil rights prosecution of a police officer for excessive use of force, a police officer who comes in to testify against a fellow police officer, when meeting with lawyers for that police officer, it's -- the best-behaved defence attorney can do everything properly, but that witness feels a subtle coercion, maybe self-induced coercion, but to be in a position of testifying against his fellow police officer or an American testifying against an American in a non-American Tribunal with non-American prosecutors on the other side. There is, I think, in real life it's human nature to feel a certain coercion and that's the point I was trying to make. And I do apologise to my friends and Your Honours. I wanted to make that statement to you. And with that, I'm ready to have the witness back in. I understand that you said you don't want me to press him any further on this, but I would like to bring out some of the things he said in his statement 2002 that I think is information that may relate to the argument about when the date occurred that -- I would just like to confirm that he said it then, and I can make my arguments at a later date. I'm not trying to harass him. I'm just trying to get that information in the record about what he said to those present, who was present, when Mr. Zugic showed up in the municipality later on, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And, if I may add, the point raised by counsel Zecevic that the dates or the time when the passage was cleared is also of some importance to this issue. So if you would wish to raise this also with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour, but I don't know how far I can get with him on that because I think he's not clear on when that date was. And that's something that hopefully there will be other evidence from other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the spirit of co-operation that we have so far in this case, I understand the -- and I of course accept the apology of Mr. Hannis. I know him for quite some time, so I know that he really didn't meant what he actually said on the record. However, I believe Your Honours have ruled on this, and I don't see that we can go now with the -- through another passage or another road around -- around about in order to get to the very same issue because again we are going to be faced with the same problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, just for the record, Your Honours, one of the golden rules of cross-examination is to know when to stop, among other rules. And unfortunately, my learned friend Mr. Hannis didn't stop. So in his just earlier explanations, he even went further on. My personal position is the following. I do not accept his apologies, point number one. Point number two, I will go through the ADC organs to inform his chief Prosecutor about his behaviour and to take necessary measures because I cannot accept this kind of swinging and then shifting explanations. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could we have the witness returned to the -- escorted back to the stand. If there is no one in the gallery, I don't know that we have to go through the ritual of lowering the shades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, while the witness is on his way in, we've heard what you propose to do, but as counsel for the Defence has said we don't see that it's going to take us any further than we are. So let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, yes, Your Honour. Part of what I intend to read to him from his previous statement relates to another area of questions of Mr. Cvijetic at page 41, line 15, was asking the witness about the nature of the information this witness informed Mr. Stanisic and Mr. Mandic about. I think it goes directly to that. And he also asked him about when Mr. Zugic showed up in the municipality, and there's another part of his statement that pertains to that. That's what I want to ask him about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, if you have that statement still in front of you, paragraph 130, still talking about the meeting in Sekovici --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, if you could wait for the noise of the blinds to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, you see that paragraph talking about the meeting, you say: "They told us about events in Sarajevo and that the Ministry of Internal Affairs was being formed." And on my next page further on in the paragraph it says: "Mico Stanisic and Momcilo Mandic were informed of the problems with the paramilitaries." And you said at that time: "I informed them about the paramilitary armies and what they were doing in a negative sense. This was before the people moved out." What you could hear in Zvornik --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- was that people had been locked up and people had been killed --

utterances.speaker: MR. CVIJETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have an objection in this manner of presentation. This is a viva voce witness and again through the side door we are bringing in that statement of his. Again, yesterday we gallantly just allowed this quoting to pass, but I think we need to have some kind of degree in terms of how much of that can be used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course Mr. Cvijetic is correct, and I noted it as well yesterday but I suppose that matter was not in controversy so no harm was done.
